subject: Using SWC files and comparing specific neurons in NBLAST

messages.author: 2c1060146d788815
messages.subject: Using SWC files and comparing specific neurons in NBLAST
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to use NBLAST to measure the similarity between dotprops made from exporting neurons from FlyWire and from light microscopy data. I would appreciate any help on navigating through the code.
I exported FlyWire neuron skeletons as an SWC file through Python by using fafbseg.flywire.skeletonize_neuron(segment ID) and navis.write_swc. I converted skeleton nrrd files from LM to dotprops through R by using dotprops("my_skeleton.nrrd", k=3). I then downloaded the dotprop as a CSV file by using write.csv(dp,file="my_dotprop.csv"). 
I am trying to run an NBLAST using the resulting SWC file as the query and the CSV file as the target. I am having trouble using the navis.make_dotprops function with the SWC file. It works fine when I try with a CSV file. Also, when I try NBLASTing with another CSV file as the query with the navis.nblast function instead, I get a message reading "'NoneType' object is not iterable". 

How can I solve these issues? Is there a way to convert between SWC and CSV, or a way to export FlyWire neurons as a CSV? How do I go about solving the "'NoneType' object is not iterable" error? I would be happy to receive any advice on this matter.

Thank you,
Amanda Abusaif

messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] Using SWC files and comparing specific neurons in NBLAST
parts:
Dear Amanda,

Thanks for your messsge. This mailing list is focussed on the R natverse packages but it looks like the problem you have is with the NAVis Python packages. Unfortunately the lead NAVis author Philipp Schlegel does not monitor it regularly — I think he prefers problems to be raised as GitHub issues. 

https://github.com/navis-org/navis

Second, you will need to give more details. Exactly what code were you running? What data were you using as input (share an example in a zip file on GitHub if necessary)? The goal is to make your problem *reproducible* with minimal effort by the developers. 

Good luck!

Greg. 


Sent from my iPhone
